description: Runs the borrow vectors against a throwaway repository with real git: a borrowed description must not leak to any background process. Red means doctor FAIL and fgctl activate refuses. There is no switch that disables borrowing at run time.

optional.meaning: run only the named vectors; default all four
keep the temporary repository for diagnosis and print its path in detail

environment.repo: a fresh temporary repository under the temp directory, removed afterwards
environment.borrowedGitArgs: every git call is made through run_borrowed, which prepends -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false
environment.lockFile: a lock file inside the temporary directory, taken EX by the vector runner

vectors.name: shell-alias-background
vectors.setup: git alias defined through config that starts a background `sleep` in the shell
vectors.assert: the lock is free (probe == free) as soon as git has exited and the owner closed its description

vectors.name: filter-clean-smudge
vectors.setup: clean/smudge filter whose script starts a background process
vectors.action: git add and git checkout of a filtered file through run_borrowed
vectors.assert: the lock is free as soon as git has exited and the owner closed its description

vectors.name: hook-background
vectors.setup: hook (pre-commit and post-commit) that starts a background process
vectors.assert: the lock is free as soon as git has exited and the owner closed its description; leftovers are killed by run_borrowed before it returns

vectors.name: gc-auto-loose-objects
vectors.setup: repository config gc.auto=1 and enough loose objects to make gc --auto eligible
vectors.assert: the lock is free as soon as git has exited and the owner closed its description; no gc process outlives the call

siblingCheck.name: sibling-refused
siblingCheck.meaning: a sibling process with the same FGOS_LOCK_FD value that opened the file itself is not a borrower (lock-fd --borrowed-check answers not-borrower)

budget.meaning: the full run stays under one second on the reference machine; exceeding it is reported in detail, not a failure by itself

exitCodes.0: pass: all vectors and the sibling check green
exitCodes.10: fail: at least one vector red
exitCodes.12: unavailable (no git, unsupported platform): treated as fail by activate
